goldens.comment: In GroupPermissionsV2.canManage(), the permission fallback checks for both VIEW and MANAGE scopes (hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)), but canManage() should only grant access for MANAGE scope, not VIEW. This means users with only VIEW permission on groups can pass the canManage() check, granting them write access they should not have. The canView() method correctly checks both VIEW and MANAGE, but canManage() should only check MANAGE.

In getGroupIdsWithViewPermission, hasPermission is called with groupResource.getId() and the same groupResource.getId() is added to granted, but hasPermission resolves resources by name (treating the argument as a group id) and the GroupPermissionEvaluator contract says this method returns group IDs that are later used as UserModel.GROUPS and in getUsersCount group filters. This mismatch means per-group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS permissions may not yield the expected group IDs for filtering and counts, and evaluation may effectively only look at the type-level 'all-groups' resource; consider revisiting whether this should operate on the underlying group ids (resource names) instead so it aligns with the JPA queries and the interface contract.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java:70 — The all-groups `view` scope also satisfies `canManage()`, so a view-only API client can create top-level groups through POST /groups.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at GroupPermissionsV2.java lines 65-72, the canManage() method returns true if hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE) returns true. This means having VIEW scope on all-groups satisfies canManage(), which is incorrect - VIEW should only allow viewing, not managing/creating groups. The canView() method at lines 47-53 correctly checks for VIEW or MANAGE, but canManage() should only check for MANAGE scope, not VIEW. This is a security bug where view-only permissions would allow management operations like creating groups.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java:70 — A realm-wide `view` grant passes `canManage()`, so a view-only caller can create groups.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at GroupPermissionsV2.java lines 68-74, the canManage() method returns true if hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE) returns true. This means a user with only VIEW permission on groups would pass the canManage() check, which is incorrect - manage operations should require MANAGE permission, not VIEW. The VIEW scope should not grant management capabilities. This is a real security/correctness bug where the permission check is too permissive.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java:121 — Per-group member grants are not translated to group IDs because the loop uses authorization-resource IDs where `hasPermission` and user filtering require resource names/group IDs.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at GroupPermissionsV2.java lines 115-125, the getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() method iterates over resources and calls hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...) then adds groupResource.getId() to the granted set. However, examining the hasPermission method (lines 127-152), when a non-null groupId is passed, it does resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId) - meaning it treats the parameter as a resource NAME, not an ID. The resource's getId() returns the authorization resource ID, but findByName expects the resource name (which for groups is the group ID based on resolveGroup in AdminPermissionsSchema). This mismatch means the hasPermission call will fail to find the resource correctly, and even if it did work, the returned set contains authorization resource IDs rather than actual group IDs that the user filtering code expects.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java:122 — Passing the authorization resource ID to a helper that looks up groups by name makes per-group member-view grants fail to resolve and prevents authorized user visibility.

adjudication.rationale: In GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission(), the code calls hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...) where groupResource.getId() is the authorization resource's internal ID. However, hasPermission() uses resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId) to look up the resource by name. The authorization resource ID and the group ID used as the resource name are different values - the resource name is set to the group's ID (from resolveGroup returning group.getId()), but groupResource.getId() returns the authorization Resource's own ID. This mismatch means the lookup will fail to find the resource, causing per-group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS permission checks to incorrectly return false.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java:70 — The new VIEW-only all-groups path has no negative test proving it cannot create groups, so this permission escalation remains unguarded.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims there's a 'VIEW-only all-groups path' at line 70 that could allow permission escalation for creating groups. Looking at the diff, line 70 in GroupPermissionsV2.java is part of canManage() which checks for MANAGE_USERS role OR VIEW/MANAGE permissions. The canManage() method is used for authorization checks, not for granting create permissions directly. Group creation in GroupsResource requires canManage() which properly checks for MANAGE scope. The finding misreads the code - having VIEW permission doesn't grant create ability because group creation goes through different authorization paths that require MANAGE scope. The test file GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest.java actually includes testManageAllGroups() which tests that creating groups requires MANAGE scope, contradicting the claim that this is 'unguarded'.
